I am requesting an immediate FULL REFUND to my original payment method and written confirmation that this case has been resolved.

Until Booking.com returns my money and properly addresses this complaint, I cannot recommend using this platform.

⚠️ My advice to other travelers: think very carefully before paying for accommodation through Booking.com. If something goes wrong with your reservation, getting proper assistance or even getting your money back can be extremely difficult.

Review Title: I would avoid this company at all…
Review Text:
I would avoid this company at all costs.

A phishing link was sent to me through Booking.com's own messaging system, and it took me finding the evidence myself to get anyone to act

I booked a London apartment through Booking.com for August. After I confirmed the reservation, a message came through Booking.com's own platform directing me to an external website to enter my card details. Booking.com's published guidance is that they never ask guests to do this.

What I then found, entirely on my own:

1. The contact number given for a London property was a US number.
2. The host did not respond for four days, not to my messages, not to Booking.com's messages, and not to a phone call Booking.com made to them.
3. The address given for the apartment is a pub. There is no apartment there.
4. The Booking.com listing page for the property is titled as a holiday cottage in Somerset, not the London apartment I had booked.

None of this was flagged by Booking.com. I found all of it. One agent even told me the property was legitimate with strong reviews, apparently reading review history that had nothing to do with what I had booked.

The support experience was worse than the fraud:

1. I was given three different timeframes in a single day. First 48 hours, then three hours, then no timeframe at all.
2. A live chat was closed on me while I still had unanswered questions.
3. One agent confirmed in writing that relocation would be arranged free of charge. A second agent confirmed relocation was guaranteed. A third then told me the approved support was €25.
4. I was told Booking.com would not book replacement accommodation directly, and that I should fund a replacement myself and claim back afterwards.
5. The alternative eventually offered was student accommodation in zone 4, priced below my original booking so that Booking.com contributed nothing at all.
6. Any shortfall would be paid as Travel Credits to spend with Booking.com, not as money.

Fraudulent listings appear on every large platform. That is not the problem. The problem is that a phishing attempt was delivered through Booking.com's own systems, that the listing did not match its own page, that none of it was detected until a customer did the work, and that the response was to offer €25 and a suggestion I pay for it myself.

Review Title: Fraudulent Advertising & selling of Car Sizes - Booking.com confirmed a 7-seater, then left my family without suitable transport days before travel
Review Text:
In February 2026 I booked and paid for a car through Booking.com specifically because the car advertised and sold clearly stated “Volvo XC90 or similar – 7 seats.”

We are travelling as three adults and three young children, so seven seats were an essential requirement of the booking.

Less than one week before our holiday, I downloaded the rental voucher and discovered that Booking.com had changed the reservation to a BMW X5 showing only 5 seats.

I immediately contacted Booking.com.

Since then, multiple members of their own team have acknowledged in writing that:

• My original Booking.com confirmation shows 7 seats.
• The vehicle currently associated with my booking is a 5-seater.
• They cannot confirm that Hertz will provide a 7-seat vehicle.

Despite acknowledging the discrepancy, Booking.com has repeatedly suggested that I:

* cancel my booking and rebook at today’s peak-season prices;
* contact their supplier in France myself;
* or arrive at Marseille Airport with three young children and simply refuse the vehicle if it is unsuitable.

None of these is a reasonable solution.

I booked six months in advance to avoid exactly this situation.

I have now spent many hours speaking to multiple agents, sending evidence repeatedly and explaining the same issue over and over again. Every representative apologises. Every representative agrees there is a problem. Yet nobody has taken ownership or provided a solution.

Five days before travel I still have no confirmation that my family will actually have transport capable of carrying all six of us.

I have retained the complete documentary evidence, including:

• the original 7-seat confirmation;
• the later 5-seat voucher;
• the full live chat transcript;
• and Booking.com’s written acknowledgements that the booking no longer matches the original confirmation.

I sincerely hope Booking.com resolves this before we travel. If they do, I will happily update this review.

At present, however, I cannot recommend using Booking.com for car hire where vehicle specifications are critical.

Review Title: Avoid Gotogate by Booking.com at All Costs
Review Text:
My experience with Gotogate by Booking.com has been one of the most frustrating and stressful travel experiences I've ever had. I strongly advise anyone considering booking through them to think twice.

Our Thai Lion Air flight was cancelled by the airline on 3 June, well in advance of our scheduled travel on 2 July. However, we were never informed by Gotogate or Booking.com that our flight had been cancelled. There was no email, no SMS, no phone call, and no attempt to offer an alternative flight or assist us in any way.

The only reason we discovered the cancellation was when we tried to complete web check-in before our trip. Imagine the shock and panic of finding out that your flight doesn't even exist just days before your vacation. Because of this complete failure in communication, we were forced to book expensive last-minute replacement tickets, costing us significantly more than what we had originally paid.

The worst part began after that. It has now been over two months, and despite countless follow-ups, we have still not received our refund. Every single time we contact Gotogate, we are given the same scripted response: "We are waiting for the airline to refund us." They refuse to take any ownership of the issue or provide any meaningful update.

To make matters worse, they repeatedly provide incorrect information, claiming that the flight was cancelled on 3 July, when in reality it was cancelled on 3 June. Even after correcting them multiple times, they continue to rely on inaccurate records instead of investigating the matter properly.

As the company that accepted my payment and issued my booking, Gotogate/Booking.com should be accountable to their customers. Passing all responsibility to the airline while leaving customers without information, assistance, or refunds is simply unacceptable. Customers should not be expected to bear the financial burden and uncertainty because an intermediary fails to do its job.

The entire experience has caused unnecessary financial loss, countless hours spent chasing customer support, and tremendous mental stress. Every interaction has felt like talking to a wall, with no accountability, no empathy, and no resolution.

I have completely lost trust in Gotogate and Booking.com for flight bookings. Saving a small amount on a ticket is not worth the risk of being abandoned when something goes wrong.

My advice to anyone considering booking flights through Gotogate or Booking.com: Don't. Book directly with the airline or use a travel agency that actually supports its customers. If your flight gets cancelled, be prepared for poor communication, endless excuses, delayed refunds, and zero accountability.

This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had, and I will never use Gotogate or Booking.com for flight bookings again. I will also actively recommend that my friends, family, and colleagues avoid them if they value their money, time, and peace of mind.

I had used Booking.com for many years and made numerous reservations through the platform. However, its conduct during the catastrophic wildfires around Arcachon has completely destroyed my confidence in the company.

Our family had booked two rooms near Arcachon Bay. At that time, the area was being affected by some of the largest wildfires in modern French history. Major access roads were closed, mass evacuations were taking place, and the Gironde authorities were asking tourists not to travel to the affected region. Arcachon Bay was effectively situated between two major fire zones.

Despite the extraordinary scale of the emergency, Booking.com apparently did not classify the area as being affected by an extreme or emergency situation. It did not issue us any meaningful warning and, when we asked for assistance, simply distanced itself from the problem.

The hotel’s position was predictable: it wanted to keep the money, even though no accommodation service was provided. But Booking.com’s attitude towards its customers was truly shocking. Its customer service merely told us that nothing could be done because the hotel refused to authorise a refund.

I am certain that our family was not the only one planning a holiday around Arcachon Bay at that time. Booking.com’s failure to recognise the seriousness of the situation and its refusal to provide any meaningful assistance are therefore extremely difficult to understand.

Booking.com was perfectly willing to act as an intermediary when accepting the reservation and benefiting commercially from it. However, when a genuine emergency occurred and its customers needed protection, the company simply stepped aside and accepted no responsibility.

After many years as a loyal customer, I can only say that Booking.com disgraced itself in this situation. Before making my next hotel reservation, I will think very carefully about whether to use Booking.com again. At the very least, travellers should not expect any real assistance from the platform when something serious goes wrong.

Booking.com is a terrible platform that had repeatedly failed me when I needed customer service

I have used Booking.com extensively, but my experience following a serious incident at a property has completely changed my view of the company.

I booked four nights at Westbury House in Windermere through Booking.com. I physically attended the property within the stated check-in period, with my luggage, and attempted to check in. Following an extraordinary confrontation with the owners, the door was closed on me while I was still standing at the threshold. I was not admitted and received none of the four nights I had paid for.

What happened afterwards with Booking.com was almost as appalling.

I spent approximately two hours making around 16 calls to Booking.com numbers in Australia, the UK and the Netherlands trying to report what had happened. Calls repeatedly disconnected, including after I had been placed on hold, meaning I had to call back, identify myself and start explaining everything again.

One agent, Mohammed, became embroiled in a pointless argument about my reservation number, despite ultimately acknowledging that he could already identify the booking. When I asked for a supervisor, he refused to escalate the call.

I called again and spoke with Christine. After I criticised the lack of empathy and customer service I was receiving, she actually told me:

“I’m hanging up on you. You have to call back. I don’t like the way you’re speaking to me.”

And she did.

Meanwhile, Booking.com was emailing me saying it had contacted the property about my complaint even though nobody had successfully taken my complete account of what had happened. I replied asking, “How can you have advised them when I have not told you a thing?” and repeatedly asked for someone to call me.

I then pursued Booking.com through email and X/Twitter, including providing a detailed written account. I was repeatedly redirected back towards the same telephone customer-service system that had already failed me.

Now comes perhaps the most disturbing part: despite my repeatedly telling Booking.com that I physically attended Westbury House and had the door closed on me at the threshold, I have apparently been recorded as a NO-SHOW.

That is simply false.

And conveniently, being classified as a no-show means I am now unable to leave a Booking.com review of the property and what happened to me there.

So I attended the property, was refused the accommodation, spent hours trying to report what happened, experienced repeated disconnections and failed escalation, sent written complaints explaining that I had attended — and I am now prevented from reviewing the property because the booking records incorrectly say I never showed up.

Whether Booking.com or the property disputes my entitlement to a refund is one issue. Whether I attended the property is another. I did attend. I was not a no-show.

A booking platform proves its value when something goes wrong. Taking a reservation and processing payment is easy. Providing meaningful assistance when a customer is standing outside accommodation they have paid for is where customer service actually matters.

In my experience, Booking.com failed spectacularly at precisely that point.

Review Text:

Because the request came through Booking.com’s trusted channels, I uploaded a scan of my driver's license. The scammers then immediately sent demands for external payments via third-party links. When I investigated further, past guest reviews exposed the horrific truth: previous guests turned up to find they had no booking, and reviews showed a horse-drawn ive in waggon in an empty field instead of a luxury Paris apartment, leaving families stranded.

Booking.com openly allowed a completely fraudulent vendor onto their platform and enabled them to use internal messaging tools to trap customers.
Because of Booking.com’s utter failure to secure their platform our family holiday is in ruins, and we are left stranded with no accommodation in Paris.

Scammers now possess my full name, home address, date of birth, email address, age and a scan of my driver's license.

I had to pay £30 for CIFAS Protective Registration to prevent fraudulent bank accounts from being opened in my name, over £20 for a replacement driver's license, and cancel my credit card.

Hours of Administrative Stress and I have had to spend hours filing criminal police reports with Action Fraud and setting up fraud monitoring. When I confronted customer support about this nightmare, the agent offered zero accountability, gave copy-paste advice on running antivirus scans, and abruptly ended the chat while I was still speaking.

Booking.com allowed criminals to exploit their internal system, handed over my personal data to fraudsters, destroyed our family holiday, and dumped 100% of the cost and stress onto me. Use this site at your own extreme risk.

Review Title: Disgraceful breach of contract. Left stranded, support hung up on me
Review Text:
Absolute nightmare experience with Booking.com. We booked a 6-person Sea View apartment three weeks ago for a holiday. The host cancelled last-minute due to overbooking. Under the UK Consumer Rights Act 2015, Booking.com is required to provide a par-to-par relocation. Instead, their support team tried to force us into a severe downgrade—splitting our group and giving 4 of us a City View room.

Because this is peak season, market rates have skyrocketed. The only true equivalent sea-view alternative left is £2,252—a £1,667 cash difference from our original £585 booking. When I refused their inferior city-view downgrade and demanded they honor their relocation policy, the customer service agent completely hung up the phone on me.

This is a clear breach of consumer protection regulations and an appalling way to treat a customer facing a travel emergency. I am proceeding to book the replacement accommodation independently to mitigate my damages. I will be recovering the full £1,667 consequential loss via a statutory Section 75 claim through my UK credit card provider and filing a formal complaint with the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) and MCOL.

Review Title: Promised a refund, now being offered Travel Credit
Review Text:
Extremely disappointing experience with Booking.com.

We booked an apartment in Nice but were informed there was a leak and were offered an alternative apartment further away from the city centre. We said we wanted to keep that option open while seeing whether something closer was available. Instead, our booking was cancelled, leaving us without accommodation and having to spend a considerable amount of time contacting Booking.com.

When we eventually spoke to a representative, we were told we could choose alternative accommodation and that Booking.com would refund the difference in price.

We selected more expensive accommodation in the centre and then received written confirmation from Booking.com stating:

“We will cover up the price difference up to the amount EUR 336.39.”

Based on both the telephone conversation and this written confirmation, we booked the more expensive accommodation, which cost €882.96. We would not have chosen accommodation at this price had we not been assured that Booking.com would cover the difference.

After our stay, Booking.com asked us to provide an invoice in order to process the reimbursement. Their subsequent email repeatedly referred to this as a refund, including:

“To proceed with your refund request…”

“We’ll be happy to move forward with your refund.”

And most clearly:

“Once we receive this, we will promptly process the refund for you.”

Despite all of this, we are now being told that the price difference will NOT be refunded and can only be provided as Booking.com Travel Credit towards a future booking.

What makes this even more frustrating is that Booking.com clearly knows the distinction between a refund and Travel Credit. In the original email, they separately stated that if we incurred “additional charges at the new place”, they could “look into adding Travel Credits to your Wallet.”

Travel Credits were therefore specifically mentioned in relation to additional charges, but NOT when Booking.com told us they would “cover” the price difference. We were also verbally told it would be a refund and subsequently received an email referring to the payment as a “refund” multiple times.

Had we been told from the outset that we would have to pay the additional cost ourselves and receive credit towards a future Booking.com reservation instead, we would NEVER have chosen the more expensive accommodation.

Customer service throughout this process has also been incredibly frustrating. Telephone waiting times are very long, getting through to someone who can actually help is extremely difficult, and we have even had calls cut off after waiting, forcing us to start the process again.

We aren't asking for anything extra. We simply want Booking.com to honour what we were repeatedly told, both verbally and in writing, and reimburse the agreed price difference, up to the €336.39 maximum confirmed in their email.

Travel Credit requiring us to book with Booking.com again is not the same as the refund we were repeatedly told we would receive.

I will happily update this review if Booking.com honours the reimbursement we were promised and resolves the matter.

Review Title: Extremely disappointing experience1 STAR — BOOKING.COM LEFT ME £5,000+ OUT OF POCKET AFTER GUEST DAMAGE with…
Review Text:
Extremely disappointing experience with Booking.com and their handling of serious property damage.

I had guests stay at my property, Monkleigh House, who caused significant damage during their stay, including serious flooding. The total damage was in excess of £5,000.

There were also issues with the number of guests. The guests arrived with more people than were included in the original reservation. Rather than cancelling their booking and ruining their stay, we tried to resolve the situation reasonably and allowed the booking to continue after agreeing that the additional guests would be paid for.

After they checked out, we discovered extensive damage to the property. We provided Booking.com with photographs, evidence and contractor information demonstrating the extent of the damage.

And what did Booking.com do?

They simply sent a payment request to the guest.

The guest said they didn't agree to pay it.

And that was effectively the end of the process.

Despite the damage being supported by evidence and the costs being thousands of pounds, Booking.com offered no meaningful solution and no effective mechanism for recovering the money.

What makes this even more frustrating is that Booking.com controls the booking process and charges commission on every reservation, yet when a guest causes thousands of pounds worth of damage, the responsibility appears to be pushed entirely back onto the property owner.

Their damage deposit system is also completely inadequate. The maximum deposit they allow for the property is nowhere near sufficient to cover serious damage. In my case, the actual loss was over £5,000.

What is the point of having a damage claim process if a guest can simply say "I don't agree" and the platform effectively washes its hands of the matter?

As a property owner, I accepted the booking through Booking.com in good faith and relied on their platform to provide a reasonable level of protection when something goes seriously wrong. Instead, I have been left with a substantial financial loss and a damaged property.

This isn't about trying to avoid paying for legitimate damage or making an unreasonable claim. The damage was real, substantial and documented.

The problem is that Booking.com's system appears to be designed to make it easy to book a property, while leaving the property owner carrying the financial risk when a guest causes serious damage.

Very disappointing treatment of property owners.

If you operate a property through Booking.com, I would strongly recommend understanding exactly how little protection you may actually have when a guest causes significant damage.

For me, this experience has seriously damaged my confidence in Booking.com as a platform for property owners.
